newsitem.title: GERMANY: Spectacular rail tunnel dig begins under Berlin.
newsitem.headline: Spectacular rail tunnel dig begins under Berlin.

text.p: Engineers on Monday began one of the most spectacular parts of the building work transforming the German capital, using water cannon to install part of a new rail tunnel which will run under Berlin's future government quarter.

The tunnel will carry a new north-south rail line as part of a project to make the city, restored to its status as capital with German unification in 1990, a major rail hub and gateway to eastern Europe.

To limit the effect on the Tiergarten park and avoid lowering the water table, the engineers are applying a new technique which involves using water cannon to swill earth out from under prefabricated concrete tunnel sections.

The first section, 37 metres (yards) long and up to 60 metres wide, began to sink into the earth on Monday and will take around three months to drop to its intended depth 23 metres below ground, the national railway company, Deutsche Bahn AG, said.

The tunnel's route will carry it almost directly underneath the Reichstag building where the German parliament will meet from 1999 onwards when it leaves Bonn, and the new chancellery, due to be built nearby.
